title: Overcome Key Organizational Hurdles
coreMove: Find the few hotspots, direct experiences, kingpins, and blockers that can tip execution through organizational resistance.
sourcePressure: Apply tipping point leadership to execution hurdles by focusing leverage on cognitive, resource, motivational, and political barriers instead of trying to move everyone evenly.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating organizational change as a morale campaign where everyone needs equal persuasion and equal resources.

sourceAnchors.name: tipping point leadership
sourceAnchors.detail: official support defines the public vocabulary around cognitive, resource, motivational, and political hurdles
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Tipping point leadership starts by naming which hurdle is actually holding the room in place: seeing, resourcing, wanting, or politics.

hook: Do not open with a competitor scoreboard, a war metaphor, or a generic market map.
Do not use A crowded market is not..., The real strategy is..., or What if growth... as reusable shells.
counterintuition: Avoid Most people assume... but actually... and The opposite is true.
Avoid turning every chapter into competition bad, creativity good.
tryThisNow: Avoid Set a timer for 60 seconds and list... as a repeated action.
Avoid generic reflect on your strategy prompts.
examples: Avoid conference-room whiteboard workshops as the default scene.
Avoid repeating mugs, markers, dosing cups, bike helmets, radiators, bus depots, classrooms, narrow kitchens, or generic dashboard scenes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: precinct radio failures and cognitive hurdles
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-safety leader whose equipment requests keep stalling
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether officers get working radios before another call goes bad
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he places the failed radio on the command desk and makes the cognitive hurdle impossible to ignore
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Static crackles from a cracked patrol radio long after the call has ended

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital discharge hotspots and cold spots
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse leader with no extra headcount
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether discharge delays keep backing up beds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she chooses to move one clerk into the discharge hotspot instead of asking for more of everything
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 11:30 a.m., Juliette counts seven charts waiting beside the discharge printer

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse shift leads and visible error accountability
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations manager whose bin errors spread through shift leads
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether errors fall without lecturing every picker
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the visible board changes kingpin behavior among shift leads before the whole floor follows
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Lars two inventory counts to notice four shift leads shaped everyone else

exampleSpecs.audience: a manager facing a protected incumbent vendor
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a better vendor survives committee politics
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she protects an ally and contains a blocker before the meeting where the old contract would normally win
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "He will call procurement before lunch," Aanya says, sliding the seating chart across the table

exampleSpecs.domain: library sorting redesign and trustee exposure
exampleSpecs.audience: a civic leader trying to fund a sorting redesign
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether trustees see the strain behind slow returns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he brings trustees into the cramped returns room during the rush so the cognitive hurdle changes before budget talk starts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The returns room has one narrow aisle and a cart already blocking the sorter

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant lunch rollout and operational hotspots
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner introducing a simplified lunch service
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a promising menu dies in execution
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts the grill is the constraint, then prep reveals the true hotspot at the garnish station
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What if the lunch bottleneck is not the grill everyone complains about?

skillTargets: name cognitive, resource, motivational, and political hurdles in scenes
choose concentrated leverage over broad persuasion

tryThisNowSpec: Name the hurdle in one stalled change: cognitive, resource, motivational, or political. Do not solve it yet.
